g_policy.reason: The banner is opt-in, the offer copy states the reward (30 minutes with no sponsored stories), declining changes nothing, and 'if the ad fails' covers a game that is not ready or a play that is not confirmed.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 30 minutes without sponsored cards, which is a feature_time reward and has no cash value.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an article-open counter reaching 3 and a return to the home feed, both app events, and no chat content is used.

g_no_free_removal.reason: Nothing free is removed, locked or capped. Sponsored cards keep showing as usual unless the user chooses to play.

g_brand_safety.reason: The offer is a banner card on s01, a screen rated safe, and it is app chrome. It is not inside a conversation and is not next to unsafe or unknown content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: This is a product_change, and the new resource (an uninterrupted read) is tied to the observed core flow f01 'Read a story' (s01 -> s02), so it meets the core-loop condition.

c2_evidence.reason: 'what makes it work here' claims a full-screen video ad from AOL after every third article. No such mechanic is in the product model, which only lists the native card in m01 and s05 as an in-article ad. The claim that the app has 'no paywall, limit, or currency' also rests on an open question (nothing was seen), not on an observation.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: No paid plan was observed, and the reward is a 30-minute window capped at 2 per day, so it gives away no subscription benefit.

c5_moment.reason: The offer appears when the reader returns to the feed after finishing a third article, which is a finished action and not the middle of a task.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn unit, the reward is granted only after the play is confirmed, and the trigger is a detectable article-open counter and screen return.

c7_specific.reason: It names the home feed sponsored card below the first story (s01.e44), the in-article card (s02.e13) and the read-then-return loop of this news app.

other_concern: Revenue is uncertain: hiding cards, some of which may be direct-sold, for 30 minutes may cost more than one game earns. The frequency cap of 2 per day is reasonable but the payoff is not proven.
